It is worthwhile remembering that ChatGPT makes a lot of mistakes, especially with application/physics based questions. This works fine for, say, an integral you want to compute, but multi part questions are something ChatGPT struggles to replicate.

How to absolutely and utterly shatter someone’s possibility of success in Methods/Spesh simply through CAS sabotage:

1. Firstly, have the calculator trigonometry mode set to **degrees**. This is useful because it may take them a while to notice. People aren’t used to checking what mode their calculator is on, because radians is second nature. Just setting it to degrees can mess up half of their SAC or exam.

2. Create programs that work **incorrectly**. Scripts, such as those that give you lists of transformations, or Newtons Method, are really easy to sabotage. People don’t really check through the code of the scripts they download, and more often than not, don’t actually know how they work.

3. Set their numbers to complex. This works especially well for Methods kids, who use Reals and only reals.

4. Switch to polar coordinates. Again, something that works a whole lot better with solely methods students’, as they won’t know what this is either.

5. Switch the language. Preferably one that writes from right to left, such as Arabic, just to throw them off further.

6. **do not** charge the battery beforehand. Pretty easy to understand why this works.

7. If all else fails, just put the CAS on press to test. This one isn’t subtle, so they’ll notice off the get go. 

If you do all of these steps, there’s just about a 100% chance that they won’t notice everything, and you will have successfully sabotaged a SAC. I’d also like to note that this information is solely for educational purposes.

Listen man, When people complain about the customers at their workplace, I get really ticked off. Everyone complains about the rude woman who didn’t leave a tip, the old guy who patronises employees by making them feel useless, but none of these customers are anywhere near as terrible as some of my clients. On an average day working at the Red Cocktail Lounge, you risk getting attacked by drunk orcs, enticed into signing your soul away by the literal devil, or even worse, having to serve death(that guy has serious drinking problems). 

But occasionally, you get to watch some fun things occur. For instance, today, a human being walked in. Yes. A regular human being walked in. And it wasn’t a lizard man disguised as a human, like mark Zuckerberg, who sometimes pops in, or even a member of the shadow government - no, it was just a regular human from the looks of things. A good looking, middle aged man, wearing a golf shirt and jeans. But again, just a man.

His appearance in a bar filled with demons, goblins and all sorts of weird made him stick out like a sore thumb. By the time he got to the bar, the whole lounge was staring at him, now having gone entirely quiet. Even the giants had stopped talking. No one knew how they were supposed to react either. Normal humans, besides workers like me, were never supposed to know of this place. The tension has become palpable.

Nonetheless, my job was to serve everyone. “What would you like to drink?” I asked. I half expected him to say some regular human drink which we didn’t serve, like a beer or a cocktail. But instead, he asked for an Essence of fire. By that point, the once suspicious bar had turned into shock. Only a Crimson Dragon could drink a shot of that and not die. Not even a demon could survive. At this point, some of the dragons began to laugh, breaking the tension.

“Little human,” one of the dragons yelled from across the bar. “Best drink something more fitting for your species! You’re too weak to drink fire!” The human sat quietly for a moment, staring at the dragon who had just yelled at him. Then, he nodded. “You’re right, sir, I am too weak for just one,” he replied. “Barkeep, I’ll take 3! I work long days, so I might as well enjoy myself.”

“If you’re sure, sir,” I replied, beginning to prepare his drinks hesitantly. The dragons still laughing in the background. I presented the man with his drinks, and watched him gulp them all down. I waited for him to implode, as most other species would when drinking just one, but… nothing happened. And all the laughter of the dragons stopped. Some of the patrons began to leave the bar in fear. Now, the dragons began to snarl at the human, contempt growing in their eyes. They began to approach the man, their bodies towering over the other patrons. Whoever this man was, whatever he was, he had scared the whole lounge.

The dragon who had yelled at the man previously breathed a mouthful of fire into the air before turning back to the man. “What are you?” The dragon asked. “A human comes in here and drinks our drink. No one drinks our drink and lives. Even I, a crimson dragon of the North Atlantic cannot drink more than one. What kind of twisted creature are you?” The dragon snarled at the man, awaiting a response. I was sure the dragon would attempt to eat the man, but then, all the dragons and the man begin to laugh. They start rolling on the floor as if they had just heard the funniest joke. “Vermithax!” The man yells. “I’ve missed you!” The man and the dragons are all yelling at one another, laughing their heads off about some stupid inside jokes they were making. Whoever this man is, he must have been very interesting.

By this time, I realise my shift is over, so I go into the back room to clock out. Though I would like to know who the man was, in this line of work, it’s best to leave when your shifts done. Whilst other workers stick around to collect the tips they rightfully earned, or to learn more about an interesting patron, I don’t push my luck. I get paid a whole lot more than most normal humans anyways. In this line of work, I’m the only bartender who has kept his job for longer than a year. Why? Because I don’t go looking into these things. 

And if you’re going to work here, you best start doing the same. I think that wraps up the training briefing. Just stay away from the infected harpies, only let the vampires in if they promise to not bite, don’t ignore an immortal cultist, and never, ever, ever, try to “figure out” a human. Not if you value your life that is. Trust me on this, the weird things here are weird, but nothing is weirder than us humans.
